name: The local:global attention layer ratio is an unmeasured structural degree of freedom
statement: Raising the proportion of short-window layers (SSSL -> SSSSLL over the depth-8 stack) trades global mixing capacity for attention FLOPs. If global mixing is currently oversupplied at depth 8, the trade is favourable under a fixed time budget; if it is undersupplied, val_bpb degrades and the direction of the effect identifies which regime the baseline is in.

nodes.label: attention FLOPs per step and the depth of first global mixing

assumptions.statement: The final layer remains full-context, so the change alters the interior mixing schedule rather than removing global attention entirely.

alternatives: Any change is explained by step count alone and carries no structural information.
predictions: The sign of the effect is informative in both directions: this experiment cannot return an uninformative null unless the delta is inside the noise band.
falsifiers: The delta is inside the measured control noise band, which would say the local:global ratio is not a live degree of freedom at this scale.
